text: Пульс уходящего дня. Главное «Между нами» Зеленский, едва не разрыдавшись, впервые признал, что чувствует себя преданным Трампом. На прямой вопрос британского телеведущего Пирса Моргана ответил: «Правда, да. Между нами». Сказано на ютуб-шоу с многомиллионной аудиторией. Украина «теряет сильного партнёра, но не из-за нас», а Трамп «не на той стороне истории». Посредником пусть будет, разрешил Зеленский, но «если ты посередине — оставайся посередине». В отставку он не собирается — хотя в субботу Трамп советовал Украине найти лидера, «который сможет договориться». Досталось и Маску: из-за урезанного Starlink, по словам Зеленского, не взлетели перехватчики и гибли люди. А радио NPR он признался, что о перемирии узнал из соцсети Трампа, «как и вы». Британская жилетка Лондон стал первой европейской столицей, куда Зеленский поехал после дизельной сделки Трампа с Москвой. Летел через польский Жешув — впервые после летнего скандала, когда Варшава отобрала у него орден Белого орла за часть, названную в честь героев УПА. 25 минут у Карла III, почётный караул на Даунинг-стрит, объятия премьера Энди Бёрнема: «Мы за вами, и это не изменится». text: 📈 О российско-китайской торговле в январе-сентябре 2026 г. США , в том числе отечественный экспорт в КНР — 116,247 млрд (+28,6%), импорт из Китая — 98,059 млрд долл. (+33,1%). В списке основных торговых партнеров Китая наша страна занимает пятую позицию . КНР уверенно удерживает лидерство среди внешнеторговых контрагентов России . Динамика двусторонних торговых связей продолжает демонстрировать уверенный восходящий тренд . text: Глава РЖД Олег Белозёров: «Мы намерены твёрдо придерживаться условий концессионного договора по железным дорогам Армении» 14 октября в ходе рабочей поездки в Ереван генеральный директор – председатель правления ОАО «РЖД» Олег Белозёров встретился с премьер-министром Республики Армения Николом Пашиняном. Темой для обсуждения стала реализация концессии по управлению железными дорогами Армении. В ходе встречи Олег Белозёров рассказал о результатах деятельности ЗАО «Южно-Кавказская железная дорога» – дочернего общества ОАО «РЖД», обеспечивающего реализацию концессионного договора, и заверил правительство Армении в лице премьер-министра в приверженности компании всем взятым обязательствам. «Задача железнодорожников – обеспечивать экономики наших стран транспортным сообщением. Концессия позволила сохранить и развивать железнодорожную инфраструктуру Армении, не перекладывая расходы на восстановление и содержание на бюджет республики. Вся прибыль шла на развитие железной дороги. Общий объём инвестиций из средств ОАО «РЖД» и доходов Южно-Кавказской железной дороги за время концессии составил 146 миллиардов армянских драм, или около 400 миллионов долларов США. text: В Росатоме успешно завершили испытания вольфрама для международного термоядерного реактора ИТЭР В НИИ электрофизической аппаратуры имени Ефремова (АО "НИИЭФА", предприятие "Росатома") успешно завершен этап квалификационных испытаний вольфрама для облицовки первой стенки международного термоядерного экспериментального реактора ИТЭР. Как сообщили в Корпорации, на этом этапе квалификационной программы подтвердились выбранные конструкторские и технологические решения. Специалисты спаяли вольфрамовые облицовки и провели ультразвуковой контроль спаянных макетов на роботизированном комплексе. По оценке директора Проектного центра ИТЭР госкорпорации "Росатом" Анатолия Красильникова, это одна из важнейших научно-исследовательских и опытно-конструкторских работ, проведённых в России в этом году. "Три года назад участники проекта приняли решение, что облицовка панелей первой стенки должна быть изготовлена из вольфрама. И перед нами встала задача перестроить всё производство на новый материал. Проведённые в Санкт-Петербурге работы — лишь начальный этап целого комплекса исследований, но их успешный результат говорит о правильно выбранном технологическом пути и наших высоких компетенциях. text: Мы — под Покровом Богородицы. Богородица — защитница и покровительница России, покрывает нас любовью и заботой. С Пречистой Девой связаны решающие моменты русской истории: чудотворная икона Казанской Божией Матери была с ополчением Минина и Пожарского. Перед Бородинским сражением русское войско обошли с чудотворным образом Смоленской Божией Матери. В 1941-м перед победой в битве за Москву вокруг столицы пролетел самолёт с чудотворной Тихвинской иконой Божией Матери. С Владимирской иконой Божьей Матери связано предание, что Богородица пришла к завоевателю Тамерлану во сне — после увиденного он отказался от похода на Москву. Русским людям Богородица являлась в Казани, в районе Августовского леса на фронтах Первой мировой, во время сражения на Курской дуге — всё это стало частью нашего духовного кода. Она приходила к Сергию Радонежскому, Серафиму Саровскому, Прокопию Устюжскому, Евфросинии Суздальской. У нас располагается один из Её земных уделов, мест особого покровительства – Дивеево. Есть даже свидетельства о помощи Девы Марии в изгнании террористов из Будённовска и защите Цхинвала. Сегодня миллионы верующих в день Покрова обращаются к Богородице за помощью и защитой – Её образ объ

title: Russian political scientist Alexander Kynev, arrested on drug charges and reportedly beaten so badly his leg was broken in two places, faces transfer to another detention center, lawyer says
text: Political scientist Alexander Kynev, who was arrested in connection with an alleged attempt to sell drugs, was due to be transferred from the Matrosskaya Tishina pretrial detention center to another detention facility on October 14, his lawyer Mikhail Biryukov said. “We don’t know why he is being transferred, on what grounds, or where he will be held,” Biryukov said. Kynev is one of the most respected experts on Russian regional politics and elections. Russian authorities have designated him a “foreign agent.” Kynev was arrested on September 25. Human rights advocates from Slovo Zashchity said he was severely beaten during his arrest. The advocates said he was diagnosed with two fractures in his shinbone. He was admitted to Matrosskaya Tishina’s hospital. According to political scientist Ekaterina Schulmann , Kynev’s leg was broken to force him to confess to treason. She did not specify where she got this information. title: Russian authorities move to evict war refugees from temporary shelters south of Moscow. Many have nowhere else to go.
text: Marina, a refugee from the Donetsk region, at a temporary accommodation center in the Tula region The Tula regional government has decided to evict residents from local temporary accommodation centers. Since 2022, the centers have housed refugees from Ukraine and Russia’s border communities. Many are single mothers with children, older people, or people who only recently escaped the fighting and have yet to find work and settle in. They cannot return home: The war continues where they lived, and many homes and even entire communities have been destroyed. Journalists from the Bereg cooperative spoke with residents of one temporary accommodation center in the Tula region about how they became refugees and what they expect after eviction. Meduza is translating their report in full. ‘We’re all pleading with you not to throw us out on the street’ The parking lot outside a health resort in the Tula region is packed with cars bearing license plate codes rarely seen here. “180” and “181” designate the annexed Donetsk and Luhansk People’s Republics. The rarest code is “188.” Those plates were issued in the Kharkiv region during the six months in 2022 when Russia occupied part of the region.

title: Ukraine detains Russian soldier after five Ukrainian troops shot dead in Kharkiv region
text: Update: The Security Service of Ukraine confirmed that the man who attacked the Ukrainian soldiers has been detained. He is a 36-year-old Russian soldier from St. Petersburg who was previously convicted in Russia. The agency did not specify whether he was a prisoner of war. Five soldiers from the Ukrainian Armed Forces’ 72nd Separate Mechanized Brigade were shot dead on October 13 in the village of Kutuzivka in the Kharkiv region. According to Ukraine’s Military Law Enforcement Service, which polices the armed forces, “a man in civilian clothes armed with an automatic weapon” opened fire. The motive remains unknown. The service said the slain soldiers had gotten along well with their comrades and had no disciplinary problems. The news outlet Hlavkom reported that police are searching for two Russian soldiers in connection with the killings. Both had escaped captivity. Law enforcement sources told Suspilne that the gunman had already been detained in a district of Kharkiv. Police and prosecutors have not yet confirmed that account. Ukrainian law enforcement authorities are considering several possible explanations for the attack and have not ruled out Russian soldiers’ involvement.

title: ‘Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government.’ Musk responds to Ukraine’s complaints about restrictions on the military version of Starlink.
text: SpaceX has restored service in Ukraine for Starlink satellite terminals moving at high speeds, former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said on the evening of October 14. “Starlink connectivity at speeds of up to 160 km/h [about 100 mph] is being restored. Removing Starshield ’s speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine’s defense. Thank you, Elon Musk. We hope for your continued support,” Fedorov said on social media. In response , Musk said Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government. “Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” Musk said. He said Starlink is a commercial service whose use is “limited to civilian or defensive activities.” Ukraine’s Defense Ministry told journalists that SpaceX still imposes a speed limit of 161 kilometers per hour (about 100 mph) on the terminals. “However, we’re currently seeing improved connection quality at speeds of up to 160 [km],” officials said. Ukrainian military personnel and officials said on the morning of October 14 that SpaceX had restricted service without warning for Starlink terminals used by Ukraine’s armed forces on the front lines. title: Yelena Morgunova, wife of Russian performance artist Pavel Krisevich, describes two arrests, threats against her family, and an ultimatum to leave Russia
text: Yelena Morgunova On October 10, protest artist Pavel Krisevich said his wife, Yelena Morgunova, had managed to leave Russia after a series of “back-to-back” arrests. Police detained Morgunova in the Ryazan region on August 28 after she returned to Russia for a brief visit with relatives. Krisevich and Morgunova had been living in France since late 2025 — they left on a humanitarian visa after the artist served two jail terms for administrative offenses. In an interview with Meduza, Morgunova spoke about her detention, life in a Paris squat, and her relationship with former Pussy Riot member Rita Flores, who recently admitted to cooperating with Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB). Warning: This article contains profanity. ‘What if they gave you some assignment — to bring in explosives?’ — Where are you now? — I’m in Europe now, on my way to Paris to join Pasha. The problem is, I can’t fly because Céline [Morgunova and Krisevich’s dog] has a short, brachycephalic snout, and there’s a risk that the pressure inside her skull could rise on a plane. title: Government Says It Helped Yandex Migrate Systems After Data Center Attacks
text: Government Says It Helped Yandex Migrate Systems After Data Center Attacks Oct. 14, 2026 REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova Russia’s Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev said Wednesday that his office helped tech giant Yandex migrate core systems to external backup servers following last week’s Ukrainian drone attacks. “The ministry assisted Yandex in providing additional sites for relocating key systems,” Shadayev told the business news outlet RBC. Yandex maintained that it has “for many years” developed distributed infrastructure and backup capacities at independent sites. Ukrainian drone attacks, which Shadayev referred to as “ unprecedented ,” damaged three of Yandex’s six data centers last week. The outages disrupted search, navigation, food delivery and banking services while also affecting corporate clients on Yandex Cloud, including retail giants like Lenta and Magnit. Key Yandex services like Pay and Cloud did not appear to be fully restored as of Wednesday evening. text: Nord Stream May Have Been Lawful Target, Argue Lawyers for Ukrainian Accused of Bombing By Reuters Oct. 14, 2026 Serhii K., a former Ukrainian army officer. Markus Scholz / Pool via REUTERS Lawyers for a Ukrainian ex-military officer accused of leading the bombing of Russia 's Nord Stream pipeline in September 2022 argued at the start of his trial in Germany on Wednesday that "an aggressor's infrastructure " may have been a lawful target . Serhii Kuznetsov is accused of leading a group of Ukrainian agents including divers and an explosives expert that blew up Russia 's largest gas pipeline to Europe in one of the biggest infrastructure sabotage operations of modern times. The case provides the first opportunity for a public hearing of evidence gathered during a years-long investigation, which has been diplomatically and politically awkward for a German government that remains staunchly supportive of Ukraine despite the investigative trail linking Kyiv to the bombing. title: Moscow Hails Trump Diesel Deal, Promises Direct Exports to U.S.
text: Moscow Hails Trump Diesel Deal, Promises Direct Exports to U.S. Oct. 14, 2026 Russia's Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak. REUTERS / Ramil Sitdikov A diesel supply deal with the United States will boost Russia’s economy and include direct exports to the U.S. market, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Wednesday. “Without a doubt, this is a positive signal for our economy,” Novak told reporters on the sidelines of the Russian Energy Week forum in Moscow, according to the state-run news agency TASS. He said the agreement would bolster oil production and refining while generating tax revenue for Russia’s state budget. Russian state agencies and oil companies are now finalizing supply contracts with U.S. counterparts, Novak said . “In accordance with the agreements, supplies will go to world markets, as well as the U.S. directly,” he said . text: Fire Spreads at Rostov Oil Terminal After Drone Attack Oct. 14, 2026 @supernova_plus / Telegram Another storage tank exploded at an oil terminal in Russia’s southern city of Rostov-on-Don late Tuesday, as a fire sparked by a drone attack continued to burn for a fourth day, monitoring channels reported. The blaze at the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery’s terminal has spread to eight of its 12 storage tanks, the independent news outlet Astra reported . The Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova+ said another tank exploded late Tuesday. Footage from the site showed tanks engulfed in flames beneath columns of black smoke. The local Telegram channel Rostov Glavny reported a bright flash on the city’s left bank at 11:50 p.m. Tuesday. Drones struck the terminal, formerly known as Yug Rusi, in Rostov’s Zheleznodorozhny district overnight on Oct. 10. title: Russia Announces Visas for Citizens of Montenegro in Reciprocal Move
text: Russia Announces Visas for Citizens of Montenegro in Reciprocal Move Oct. 14, 2026 Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Moskva News Agency Russia will introduce visa requirements for citizens of Montenegro in retaliation to Podgorica’s decision to end its bilateral visa-free travel agreement with Moscow as it seeks to join the EU in 2028. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova confirmed that Montenegro’s foreign ministry notified Moscow of its intent to cancel the 2008 mutual travel agreement on Sept. 28. “In practice, this means that starting Nov. 1, our citizens will only be able to enter and remain in Montenegro with visas. Accordingly, citizens of Montenegro will also have to obtain visas for trips to Russia,” Zakharova said. Montenegro announced in July that it would end visa-free access for citizens of Russia, Belarus, China, Saudi Arabia and Turkey to align with EU standards. Zakharova argued the decision would curb Russian tourism, harm local businesses and degrade Montenegro’s investment climate. text: Putin Convenes Top Russian Officials to Discuss Cybersecurity By Reuters Oct. 14, 2026 kremlin.ru Russia n President Vladimir Putin will discuss cybersecurity with top officials on Wednesday, the Kremlin said, describing it as an increasingly pressing issue but denying the meeting was prompted by a spate of Ukrainian drone attacks on Russia n data centers. "Artificial intelligence technologies bring many benefits and advantages, boosting efficiency. But at the same time, of course, attempts by various states to weaponize these new technologies... pose threats to entire sectors of any country's economy," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters. "Naturally, we are no exception, and we must be prepared for these challenges. That is why the president is holding this meeting today." news Ukraine’s Strikes on Yandex Data Centers, Explained Read more Peskov said the meeting was not connected with Ukrainian drone strikes in the past week on four Russia n data centers — three belonging to tech group Yandex and one to Sberbank. text: Russian Supreme Court Bans Ingush Sufi Muslim Order as ‘Extremist’ Oct. 14, 2026 right-partner.ru Russia’s Supreme Court on Wednesday outlawed the Batal Hajji brotherhood , a closed Sufi Muslim order originating from the North Caucasus republic of Ingushetia. The court granted a request from state prosecutors to designate the order as an “extremist” organization for “providing material support for bandit insurgents of the North Caucasus.” The Prosecutor General’s Office said Batal Hajji members were linked to numerous attacks on Russian police and military in the North Caucasus and orchestrated the deadly 2009 Nevsky Express train bombing claimed by Chechen rebel leader Doku Umarov. title: Latvia Formally Blacklists Russian Journalist Leonid Ragozin
text: Latvia Formally Blacklists Russian Journalist Leonid Ragozin Oct. 14, 2026 Leonid Ragozin. Social media Latvian authorities have formally declared Riga-based Russian journalist Leonid Ragozin persona non grata, local media reported, and Ragozin himself confirmed on Wednesday. Latvian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Līga Jermacāne told the outlet Delfi that an unidentified Russian national was added to the persona non grata list last Wednesday. Foreign Ministry adviser Toms Sadovskis said the basis for the decision will be withheld for “national security” reasons. On Wednesday, Ragozin confirmed that he was notified of his expulsion the day before. Ragozin claimed he was blacklisted in retaliation for his critical reporting and commentary on Western policy and far-right political networks. He argued that Latvia intentionally declared him persona non grata to prevent him from appealing his expulsion in Latvian courts. “For me it is a huge personal tragedy. I am being evicted from my only beloved home, deprived of my circle of friendship and support,” Ragozin posted on X. title: Russia Fumes as Top Gymnasts Blocked From World Championships in Netherlands
text: Russia Fumes as Top Gymnasts Blocked From World Championships in Netherlands Oct. 14, 2026 Angelina Melnikova. Yasuyoshi Chiba / AFP Russia has accused Dutch authorities of denying visas to three of Russia’s leading female gymnasts for the World Championships in Rotterdam, which kick off this weekend, and jeopardizing their qualification path for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Reigning world all-around champion Angelina Melnikova, Tokyo 2020 team Olympic champion Viktoria Listunova and 2026 European silver medalist Anna Kalmykova have all reportedly been refused visas, the Russian Gymnastics Federation said Tuesday, citing the Dutch Embassy in Moscow. The refusal notices apparently expressed diplomatic concerns, stating that “one or several Schengen member states consider the athletes a threat to their international relations.” “We view the actions of the Dutch authorities as a deliberate elimination of the strongest gymnasts from competition for world medals and Olympic quotas,” the Russian Gymnastics Federation said. title: Russia Arrests Japanese Journalist on Suspicion of Spying
text: Russia Arrests Japanese Journalist on Suspicion of Spying By Reuters Oct. 14, 2026 Screenshot / Russian Federal Security Service Russia said on Tuesday it had detained a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage and accused Tokyo of using media correspondents to gather intelligence, marking a new low in bilateral relations that have deteriorated sharply in recent months. Russia's Foreign Ministry identified the journalist as Yuki Imai and the FSB security agency said he worked for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, which is a regional newspaper for Japan's northern island. He was detained in the far eastern Sakhalin region the day before he planned to leave the country, the FSB said without specifying the date. It accused him of collecting and storing information on Russia's defense capabilities for intelligence purposes that it said could be used against Russian security. The Hokkaido Shimbun did not confirm the journalist's identity, saying only that it was still confirming details and that the reporter's safety was its top priority. text: Ukraine Accuses SpaceX of Crippling Drone Missions as Ties With U.S. Worsen By Reuters Oct. 14, 2026 Mil.gov.ua Ukraine accused Elon Musk's SpaceX on Wednesday of limiting Starlink services, crippling its drones, as Russia n missiles knocked out power stations in attacks President Volodymyr Zelensky called "ostentatious disrespect" to Donald Trump. Kyiv's relationship with Washington has taken a sharp turn for the worse since U.S. President Trump abruptly lifted sanctions on Russia n diesel last week and publicly turned on Zelensky. Trump, under political pressure to lower fuel prices that have soared since he launched a war against Iran, has called on Kyiv to halt attacks on Russia n refineries, and said Ukrainians should replace their wartime leader. The U.S. president also announced that Ukraine and Russia had both agreed to halt attacks on energy targets, although neither side confirmed this and the past two days have seen intensive Russia n bombing, including of Ukrainian power stations. title: Russia’s Krasnodar Region Raises Alert as Oil Washes Ashore on Black Sea Coast
text: Russia’s Krasnodar Region Raises Alert as Oil Washes Ashore on Black Sea Coast Oct. 14, 2026 @lifeabrau / Telegram Authorities in Russia’s southern Krasnodar region have raised the alert level in Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk over an oil spill after fuel oil washed ashore and satellite images showed pollution spreading along the Black Sea coast. Governor Veniamin Kondratyev issued an order warning of a potential emergency in the two cities. He attributed the spill to “accidents” involving vessels targeted by Ukrainian naval drones on Oct. 6. The order calls for increased environmental monitoring and surveillance of potential industrial hazards. It also recommends that the regional branch of Russia’s Marine Rescue Service take measures to prevent oil from reaching the shoreline. Fuel oil has already been found along roughly 500 meters of coastline near Novorossiysk, the city’s chief rescue official, Alexei Oderov, said . Local residents have also reported pollution on the shore. Olga Kotlyar, head of the Abrau-Dyurso rural district, appealed for volunteers to help municipal workers clean up a beach. text: Ukrainian Drones Hit Sberbank Data Center After Yandex Attacks Oct. 14, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram Ukrainian drones targeted a major data center under construction for Russian state lender Sberbank in the Saratov region overnight, First Deputy CEO Alexander Vedyakhin said Wednesday, as attacks on Moscow disrupted more than 500 flights. Vedyakhin said all banking systems and online services continued to operate normally and no employees were injured in the attack in the Volga River city of Balakovo, according to the state-run news agency TASS. Users across Russia nevertheless reported disruptions to Sberbank and its GigaChat artificial intelligence service, as well as several other major online platforms, according to outage tracker Detector404. The reports did not establish a link between the disruptions and the drone attacks. NASA’s satellite fire-monitoring system showed multiple fires in Balakovo. Saratov region Governor Roman Busargin said “all infrastructure facilities” were operating normally, without identifying Sberbank’s data center as a target. title: Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters
text: Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Close Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed President Volodymyr Zelensky to Downing Street on Wednesday, as the Ukrainian leader looks to shore up his European allies five years into Russia's war on Ukraine. Burnham told Zelensky that Britain "would forever stand by you" and that he was accelerating the delivery of air defences to Ukraine. Burnham previously told MPs that he would try to "repair bridges" between Ukraine and the United States and that Ukraine won't leave "empty-handed". The two leaders met at No 10 Downing Street where Zelensky was welcomed with a military ceremonial guard - thought to be a first for a foreign leader. BBC World News correspondent Joe Inwood explains what we know about the meeting. Read more about the meeting in London. text: Burnham treads carefully with Zelensky visit, balancing Trump and Ukraine Figure caption, Watch: Burnham welcomes Zelensky to No 10 with military ceremonial guard By James Landale Diplomatic correspondent Published 14 October 2026, 15:30 BST Updated 2 hours ago President Volodymyr Zelensky's visit to London follows a well-trodden diplomatic path in a war now in its fifth year. For months, US President Donald Trump had been a largely benign presence in the conflict, promising Ukraine greater access to American air defence technology and threatening more sanctions on Russia. Then last week Trump carried out an abrupt U-turn, lifting sanctions on Russian diesel and calling for Zelensky to be replaced. Once again Ukraine's leader got on his plane to shore up support among European allies. Today London, tomorrow Brussels. title: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
text: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Serhii Kuznetsov (C) was pictured in court on Wednesday as the trial got under way By Jessica Parker ,Â Berlin correspondent in Hamburg Â and Â Paul Kirby ,Â Europe digital editor Published 14 October 2026, 00:42 BST Updated 9 hours ago A Ukrainian man has gone on trial in Hamburg accused of blowing up Russia's Nord Stream gas pipelines to Germany, four years after one of the most dramatic acts of sabotage in modern European history. Prosecutors say Serhii Kuznetsov played a leading role in a team of saboteurs that destroyed the pipelines, accusing him of a war crime. His defence has called for the case to be dismissed. The case is highly sensitive in Germany, one of Ukraine's closest allies since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, seven months before the attacks took place. Extradited to Germany last year, Kuznetsov denies the charges, as does a second suspect who is fighting extradition from Croatia. text: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine war linked to political situation, Zelensky aide says Figure caption, Watch: What we know about Russia's overnight strikes on Ukraine By Jaroslav Lukiv Â and Â Dan Johnson ,Â Ukraine correspondent in Kyiv Published 14 October 2026, 08:21 BST Updated 9 hours ago New restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to the Starlink internet network have disrupted Ukraine's battlefield "missions", President Volodymyr Zelensky's adviser has warned. Serhiy Beskrestnov said Ukraine had not been told about speed limits set overnight at 100mph (160km/h) by Elon Musk's SpaceX company. Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to effectively guide drones to Russian targets and also protect Ukrainian skies. Beskrestnov said SpaceX's move "cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation". The firm has not commented. title: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine
text: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Close A key energy facility and a residential building in the outskirts of Kyiv have been hit by overnight Russian missile and drone strikes. In the capital, at least three people were killed and 21 injured, Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS said. At least 600,000 people across the country are without electricity after strikes hit critical infrastructure in the Kyiv region and the north-eastern city of Kharkiv. The strikes come after US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that an "energy ceasefire" was in place between Russia and Ukraine. Russia's defence ministry said its "massive" strikes had targeted communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military. BBC Ukraine Correspondent Dan Johnson explains. title: Australian politics live: Paterson accuses Labor of ‘contempt’ for senate over private health rebate bill; AEC warns about AI
text: 17.50 EDT ‘If you show contempt for the Senate, contempt is returned’: Paterson The Coalition says the government’s “cruel” cuts to private health insurance rebates for over-65s will fail again unless “the Greens buckle”. Frontbencher James Paterson tells News24 “good luck” to Mark Butler if he wants to try introducing that legislation again with no changes. The Greens want pensioners carved out of the changes – which would significantly diminish the budget savings from the policy. Well good luck with that, Mark Butler. In my experience, if you show contempt for the Senate, that contempt is returned, and so it should be in this case, because this is a particularly cruel cut, a cut of $3bn to older Australians who are taking out private health insurance, and in doing so, taking pressure off the public system. title: Student protests in Albania turn violent as demonstrators clash with police
text: 1:14 Anti-government student protests in Albania turn violent – video Albania Student protests in Albania turn violent as demonstrators clash with police Government building and two banks set on fire as tens of thousands march over education costs and corruption Guardian staff and agencies in Tirana Wed 14 Oct 2026 13.21 EDT First published on Wed 14 Oct 2026 13.10 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Tens of thousands of students have taken to the streets of Tirana, the Albanian capital, setting alight a government building and two banks and hurling stones at police during a protest over rising education costs and ⁠corruption. Police responded with water ⁠cannon and teargas to disperse protesters who started a fire at the ministry of education building, overturned bins and smashed the fronts of local businesses. A branch of Raiffeisen Bank near the education ministry also caught fire. The protests are the most violent outburst yet against Edi Rama, ⁠the prime minister, who won a fourth term in office in May last year but has since faced ​growing discontent at perceived graft surrounding top ‌officials. Protesters also dismiss opposition figures ‌as unpalatable alternatives. Vie

title: Trump tries to rally support for Republican candidates as top Super Pac for Senate Democrats pours millions into key races – live
text: 14.41 EDT Top Senate Democratic Super Pac pours millions more in Michigan and Maine races The top Super Pac for Senate Democrats will pour more than $7m into two marquee races this cycle: Michigan and Maine. The Senate Majority Pac has reserved $3.7m for its campaign in Michigan, to support the Democratic nominee , Dr Abdul El-Sayed , against the Trump-backed Republican, Mike Rogers . The group is also investing $3m in Maine , to boost Democrat Troy Jackson’s chances against Susan Collins – the five-term moderate GOP incumbent, who Democrats see as increasingly vulnerable in a cycle where anti-Trump sentiment has colored much of the election. This comes after reports that the Senate Majority Pac has also paused ad spending in North Carolina and Georgia. Semafor was first to report on the updated spend.

text: Справедливости ради стоит сказать, что слово блэкаут [в контексте удара по Киеву] подразумевает отсутствие света примерно везде, хотя бы в пределах обозначенной к атаке территории. Пока этого блэкаута не наблюдается, а значит без продолжения ударов не обойтись. Частично проблема в том, что подстанция 750 кВ (например, Киевская, в которую прилетает не первый раз) — это гигантский объект, занимающий десятки гектаров . Все ключевые узлы (автотрансформаторы, выключатели, разъединители) разнесены на значительные расстояния друг от друга из-за требований воздушной изоляции. Ракета или дрон могут уничтожить конкретную точку, но не могут «стереть» всю подстанцию одним или несколькими ударами, поскольку там всегда наготове стоят ремонтные бригады. Самый критичный и дорогой элемент подстанции — это группа однофазных автотрансформаторов 750 кВ. Они состоят из толстой высокопрочной стали, заполненной десятками тонн трансформаторного масла. Пробить такой бак осколками или попасть дроном, несмотря на размер устройства, сложно. Дроны-камикадзе несут сравнительно небольшой заряд (обычно 20–50 кг). text: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Serhii Kuznetsov (C) was pictured in court on Wednesday as the trial got under way By Jessica Parker ,Â Berlin correspondent in Hamburg Â and Â Paul Kirby ,Â Europe digital editor Published 14 October 2026 A Ukrainian man has gone on trial in Hamburg accused of blowing up Russia's Nord Stream gas pipelines to Germany, four years after one of the most dramatic acts of sabotage in modern European history. Prosecutors say Serhii Kuznetsov played a leading role in a team of saboteurs that destroyed the pipelines, accusing him of a war crime. His defence has called for the case to be dismissed. text: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Close A key energy facility and a residential building in the outskirts of Kyiv have been hit by overnight Russian missile and drone strikes. text: Authorities and Legislation The government has submitted to the State Duma [lower house of the Federal Assembly of Russia] a bill that would raise the maximum age for women in military service from 45 to 50 . The bill also proposes raising the maximum age for women serving in the reserve from 50 to 55 for those holding officer ranks , and from 45 to 50 for those with other military ranks . The explanatory note says the changes are intended to provide additional social guarantees, arguing that the current age limits do not always allow service members to complete the required years of service to qualify for pensions and other benefits. The Ministry of Defense has drafted a decree that would expand the powers of the military police . Commanders of military police units would be authorized to conduct preliminary inquiries into alleged crimes committed by service members, volunteers and civilian personnel. To track down servicemen who have gone AWOL, the military police would be permitted to deploy search-and-detention teams, ambushes, cordons, observation posts and patrols , as well as pursue wanted servicemen and seal off areas where they may be hiding. REUTERS / Ramil Sitdikov A diesel supply deal with the United States will boost Russia’s economy and include direct exports to the U.S. market, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Wednesday. “Without a doubt, this is a positive signal for our economy,” Novak told reporters on the sidelines of the Russian Energy Week forum in Moscow, according to the state-run news agency TASS. He said the agreement would bolster oil production and refining while generating tax revenue for Russia’s state budget. Russian state agencies and oil companies are now finalizing supply contracts with U.S. counterparts, Novak said . “In accordance with the agreements, supplies will go to world markets, as well as the U.S. directly,” he said . title: Russia Announces Visas for Citizens of Montenegro in Reciprocal Move
text: Russia Announces Visas for Citizens of Montenegro in Reciprocal Move Oct. 14, 2026 Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Moskva News Agency Russia will introduce visa requirements for citizens of Montenegro in retaliation to Podgorica’s decision to end its bilateral visa-free travel agreement with Moscow as it seeks to join the EU in 2028. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova confirmed that Montenegro’s foreign ministry notified Moscow of its intent to cancel the 2008 mutual travel agreement on Sept. 28. “In practice, this means that starting Nov. 1, our citizens will only be able to enter and remain in Montenegro with visas. Accordingly, citizens of Montenegro will also have to obtain visas for trips to Russia,” Zakharova said. Montenegro announced in July that it would end visa-free access for citizens of Russia, Belarus, China, Saudi Arabia and Turkey to align with EU standards. Zakharova argued the decision would curb Russian tourism, harm local businesses and degrade Montenegro’s investment climate. text: Latvia Formally Blacklists Russian Journalist Leonid Ragozin Oct. 14, 2026 Leonid Ragozin. Social media Latvian authorities have formally declared Riga-based Russian journalist Leonid Ragozin persona non grata, local media reported, and Ragozin himself confirmed on Wednesday. Latvian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Līga Jermacāne told the outlet Delfi that an unidentified Russian national was added to the persona non grata list last Wednesday. Foreign Ministry adviser Toms Sadovskis said the basis for the decision will be withheld for “national security” reasons. On Wednesday, Ragozin confirmed that he was notified of his expulsion the day before. Ragozin claimed he was blacklisted in retaliation for his critical reporting and commentary on Western policy and far-right political networks. He argued that Latvia intentionally declared him persona non grata to prevent him from appealing his expulsion in Latvian courts. “For me it is a huge personal tragedy. title: Russia Arrests Japanese Journalist on Suspicion of Spying
text: Russia Arrests Japanese Journalist on Suspicion of Spying By Reuters Oct. 14, 2026 Screenshot / Russian Federal Security Service Russia said on Tuesday it had detained a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage and accused Tokyo of using media correspondents to gather intelligence, marking a new low in bilateral relations that have deteriorated sharply in recent months. Russia's Foreign Ministry identified the journalist as Yuki Imai and the FSB security agency said he worked for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, which is a regional newspaper for Japan's northern island. He was detained in the far eastern Sakhalin region the day before he planned to leave the country, the FSB said without specifying the date. It accused him of collecting and storing information on Russia's defense capabilities for intelligence purposes that it said could be used against Russian security. The Hokkaido Shimbun did not confirm the journalist's identity, saying only that it was still confirming details and that the reporter's safety was its top priority. title: Russia’s Krasnodar Region Raises Alert as Oil Washes Ashore on Black Sea Coast
text: Russia’s Krasnodar Region Raises Alert as Oil Washes Ashore on Black Sea Coast Oct. 14, 2026 @lifeabrau / Telegram Authorities in Russia’s southern Krasnodar region have raised the alert level in Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk over an oil spill after fuel oil washed ashore and satellite images showed pollution spreading along the Black Sea coast. Governor Veniamin Kondratyev issued an order warning of a potential emergency in the two cities. He attributed the spill to “accidents” involving vessels targeted by Ukrainian naval drones on Oct. 6. The order calls for increased environmental monitoring and surveillance of potential industrial hazards. It also recommends that the regional branch of Russia’s Marine Rescue Service take measures to prevent oil from reaching the shoreline. Fuel oil has already been found along roughly 500 meters of coastline near Novorossiysk, the city’s chief rescue official, Alexei Oderov, said . Local residents have also reported pollution on the shore. Olga Kotlyar, head of the Abrau-Dyurso rural district, appealed for volunteers to help municipal workers clean up a beach. title: Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters
text: Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Close Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed President Volodymyr Zelensky to Downing Street on Wednesday, as the Ukrainian leader looks to shore up his European allies five years into Russia's war on Ukraine. Burnham told Zelensky that Britain "would forever stand by you" and that he was accelerating the delivery of air defences to Ukraine. Burnham previously told MPs that he would try to "repair bridges" between Ukraine and the United States and that Ukraine won't leave "empty-handed". The two leaders met at No 10 Downing Street where Zelensky was welcomed with a military ceremonial guard - thought to be a first for a foreign leader. title: Burnham treads carefully with Zelensky visit, balancing Trump and Ukraine
text: Burnham treads carefully with Zelensky visit, balancing Trump and Ukraine Figure caption, Watch: Burnham welcomes Zelensky to No 10 with military ceremonial guard By James Landale Diplomatic correspondent Published 14 October 2026 President Volodymyr Zelensky's visit to London follows a well-trodden diplomatic path in a war now in its fifth year. For months, US President Donald Trump had been a largely benign presence in the conflict, promising Ukraine greater access to American air defence technology and threatening more sanctions on Russia. Then last week Trump carried out an abrupt U-turn, lifting sanctions on Russian diesel and calling for Zelensky to be replaced. title: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
text: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Serhii Kuznetsov (C) was pictured in court on Wednesday as the trial got under way By Jessica Parker ,Â Berlin correspondent in Hamburg Â and Â Paul Kirby ,Â Europe digital editor Published 14 October 2026 A Ukrainian man has gone on trial in Hamburg accused of blowing up Russia's Nord Stream gas pipelines to Germany, four years after one of the most dramatic acts of sabotage in modern European history. Prosecutors say Serhii Kuznetsov played a leading role in a team of saboteurs that destroyed the pipelines, accusing him of a war crime. His defence has called for the case to be dismissed. The case is highly sensitive in Germany, one of Ukraine's closest allies since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, seven months before the attacks took place. Extradited to Germany last year, Kuznetsov denies the charges, as does a second suspect who is fighting extradition from Croatia. text: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine war linked to political situation, Zelensky aide says Figure caption, Watch: What we know about Russia's overnight strikes on Ukraine By Jaroslav Lukiv Â and Â Dan Johnson ,Â Ukraine correspondent in Kyiv Published 14 October 2026 New restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to the Starlink internet network have disrupted Ukraine's battlefield "missions", President Volodymyr Zelensky's adviser has warned. Serhiy Beskrestnov said Ukraine had not been told about speed limits set overnight at 100mph (160km/h) by Elon Musk's SpaceX company. Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to effectively guide drones to Russian targets and also protect Ukrainian skies. title: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine
text: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Close A key energy facility and a residential building in the outskirts of Kyiv have been hit by overnight Russian missile and drone strikes. In the capital, at least three people were killed and 21 injured, Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS said. At least 600,000 people across the country are without electricity after strikes hit critical infrastructure in the Kyiv region and the north-eastern city of Kharkiv. The strikes come after US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that an "energy ceasefire" was in place between Russia and Ukraine. Russia's defence ministry said its "massive" strikes had targeted communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military. BBC Ukraine Correspondent Dan Johnson explains. title: Ukrainian drones are hitting Russia’s biggest data centers. Why are they so vulnerable — and can anything protect them?
text: news Ukrainian drones are hitting Russia’s biggest data centers. Why are they so vulnerable — and can anything protect them? October 14, 2026, 2:37 pm Source: Meduza A Yandex data center in Vladimir. 2019. HAKA Moscow After strikes on Yandex’s data centers, pro-war channels accused the company of inaction and even sabotage. Elements of critical infrastructure turned out to be completely unprotected against drone attacks. Now similar accusations will likely be directed at Sberbank: the bank’s largest data center in the Saratov region was attacked overnight on October 14. All these facilities were an obvious target for Ukraine’s military, if only because Russian forces are actively striking similar targets in Ukraine. Of course, the inadequate protection of the data centers has nothing to do with malicious intent or negligence on the part of Yandex and Sberbank’s management. It is known that, even before the strikes, authorities and the military discussed measures to defend such facilities with businesses. title: Government Says It Helped Yandex Migrate Systems After Data Center Attacks
text: Government Says It Helped Yandex Migrate Systems After Data Center Attacks Oct. 14, 2026 REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova Russia’s Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev said Wednesday that his office helped tech giant Yandex migrate core systems to external backup servers following last week’s Ukrainian drone attacks. “The ministry assisted Yandex in providing additional sites for relocating key systems,” Shadayev told the business news outlet RBC. Yandex maintained that it has “for many years” developed distributed infrastructure and backup capacities at independent sites. Ukrainian drone attacks, which Shadayev referred to as “ unprecedented ,” damaged three of Yandex’s six data centers last week. The outages disrupted search, navigation, food delivery and banking services while also affecting corporate clients on Yandex Cloud, including retail giants like Lenta and Magnit. Key Yandex services like Pay and Cloud did not appear to be fully restored as of Wednesday evening. text: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Close A key energy facility and a residential building in the outskirts of Kyiv have been hit by overnight Russian missile and drone strikes. In the capital, at least three people were killed and 21 injured, Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS said. At least 600,000 people across the country are without electricity after strikes hit critical infrastructure in the Kyiv region and the north-eastern city of Kharkiv. The strikes come after US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that an "energy ceasefire" was in place between Russia and Ukraine. text: Russia Announces Visas for Citizens of Montenegro in Reciprocal Move Oct. 14, 2026 Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Moskva News Agency Russia will introduce visa requirements for citizens of Montenegro in retaliation to Podgorica’s decision to end its bilateral visa-free travel agreement with Moscow as it seeks to join the EU in 2028. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova confirmed that Montenegro’s foreign ministry notified Moscow of its intent to cancel the 2008 mutual travel agreement on Sept. 28. “In practice, this means that starting Nov. 1, our citizens will only be able to enter and remain in Montenegro with visas. Accordingly, citizens of Montenegro will also have to obtain visas for trips to Russia,” Zakharova said. Montenegro announced in July that it would end visa-free access for citizens of Russia, Belarus, China, Saudi Arabia and Turkey to align with EU standards. Zakharova argued the decision would curb Russian tourism, harm local businesses and degrade Montenegro’s investment climate. text: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Close A key energy facility and a residential building in the outskirts of Kyiv have been hit by overnight Russian missile and drone strikes. text: The French anti-terrorism prosecutor has taken ​over the investigation into a school shooting near Marseille, after an initial probe found the 14-year-old suspect appeared to belong to ​a ‌group called the True Crime ⁠Community. title: Burnham treads carefully with Zelensky visit, balancing Trump and Ukraine
text: Burnham treads carefully with Zelensky visit, balancing Trump and Ukraine Figure caption, Watch: Burnham welcomes Zelensky to No 10 with military ceremonial guard By James Landale Diplomatic correspondent Published 14 October 2026 President Volodymyr Zelensky's visit to London follows a well-trodden diplomatic path in a war now in its fifth year. For months, US President Donald Trump had been a largely benign presence in the conflict, promising Ukraine greater access to American air defence technology and threatening more sanctions on Russia. Then last week Trump carried out an abrupt U-turn, lifting sanctions on Russian diesel and calling for Zelensky to be replaced. Once again Ukraine's leader got on his plane to shore up support among European allies. Today London, tomorrow Brussels. Image source, PA Image caption, "We are behind you and that will not change," Burnham told Zelensky For the prime minister there was the tricky but now familiar diplomatic task of needing to show solidarity with Zelensky without appearing to criticise Trump. Burnham's answer was to say and announce as much as he could without exposing himself to questions from journalists asking about Trump's latest

title: Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters
text: Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Close Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed President Volodymyr Zelensky to Downing Street on Wednesday, as the Ukrainian leader looks to shore up his European allies five years into Russia's war on Ukraine. Burnham told Zelensky that Britain "would forever stand by you" and that he was accelerating the delivery of air defences to Ukraine. Burnham previously told MPs that he would try to "repair bridges" between Ukraine and the United States and that Ukraine won't leave "empty-handed". The two leaders met at No 10 Downing Street where Zelensky was welcomed with a military ceremonial guard - thought to be a first for a foreign leader. BBC World News correspondent Joe Inwood explains what we know about the meeting. Read more about the meeting in London. title: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine war linked to political situation, Zelensky aide says
text: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine war linked to political situation, Zelensky aide says Figure caption, Watch: What we know about Russia's overnight strikes on Ukraine By Jaroslav Lukiv Â and Â Dan Johnson ,Â Ukraine correspondent in Kyiv Published 14 October 2026 New restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to the Starlink internet network have disrupted Ukraine's battlefield "missions", President Volodymyr Zelensky's adviser has warned. Serhiy Beskrestnov said Ukraine had not been told about speed limits set overnight at 100mph (160km/h) by Elon Musk's SpaceX company. title: India’s cockroach protesters defy Modi’s crackdown – The Latest
text: 00:00:00 00:00:00 Today in Focus India India’s cockroach protesters defy Modi’s crackdown – The Latest A fresh wave of protests by India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has been met with a brutal crackdown by Narendra Modi’s government and the closure of a historic protest site in Delhi. Two of the movement’s leaders have been imprisoned for five days for violating suppression measures. The protests, which began over frustration about education and unemployment, are now focused on voting rights. Modi’s government denies claims it is seeking to disenfranchise millions of voters. But its treatment of protesters has been criticised by the UN and Amnesty International and raised concerns that India is sliding further into autocracy. title: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine
text: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Close A key energy facility and a residential building in the outskirts of Kyiv have been hit by overnight Russian missile and drone strikes. In the capital, at least three people were killed and 21 injured, Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS said. At least 600,000 people across the country are without electricity after strikes hit critical infrastructure in the Kyiv region and the north-eastern city of Kharkiv. The strikes come after US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that an "energy ceasefire" was in place between Russia and Ukraine. Russia's defence ministry said its "massive" strikes had targeted communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military. BBC Ukraine Correspondent Dan Johnson explains. Russia's Foreign Ministry identified the journalist as Yuki Imai and the FSB security agency said he worked for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, which is a regional newspaper for Japan's northern island. He was detained in the far eastern Sakhalin region the day before he planned to leave the country, the FSB said without specifying the date. text: Russia’s Krasnodar Region Raises Alert as Oil Washes Ashore on Black Sea Coast Oct. 14, 2026 @lifeabrau / Telegram Authorities in Russia’s southern Krasnodar region have raised the alert level in Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk over an oil spill after fuel oil washed ashore and satellite images showed pollution spreading along the Black Sea coast. Governor Veniamin Kondratyev issued an order warning of a potential emergency in the two cities. He attributed the spill to “accidents” involving vessels targeted by Ukrainian naval drones on Oct. 6. The order calls for increased environmental monitoring and surveillance of potential industrial hazards. It also recommends that the regional branch of Russia’s Marine Rescue Service take measures to prevent oil from reaching the shoreline. Fuel oil has already been found along roughly 500 meters of coastline near Novorossiysk, the city’s chief rescue official, Alexei Oderov, said . text: Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Close Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed President Volodymyr Zelensky to Downing Street on Wednesday, as the Ukrainian leader looks to shore up his European allies five years into Russia's war on Ukraine. Burnham told Zelensky that Britain "would forever stand by you" and that he was accelerating the delivery of air defences to Ukraine. Burnham previously told MPs that he would try to "repair bridges" between Ukraine and the United States and that Ukraine won't leave "empty-handed". The two leaders met at No 10 Downing Street where Zelensky was welcomed with a military ceremonial guard - thought to be a first for a foreign leader. Burnham told Zelensky that Britain "would forever stand by you" and that he was accelerating the delivery of air defences to Ukraine. Serhiy Beskrestnov said Ukraine had not been told about speed limits set overnight at 100mph (160km/h) by Elon Musk's SpaceX company. Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to effectively guide drones to Russian targets and also protect Ukrainian skies. Beskrestnov said SpaceX's move "cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation". The firm has not commented. In Wednesday's post on Telegram, Beskrestnov said that SpaceX had "implemented overnight a speed limit on Starlink terminals" and this had already resulted in "the disruption of a number of missions". title: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine
text: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine Close A key energy facility and a residential building in the outskirts of Kyiv have been hit by overnight Russian missile and drone strikes. In the capital, at least three people were killed and 21 injured, Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS said. At least 600,000 people across the country are without electricity after strikes hit critical infrastructure in the Kyiv region and the north-eastern city of Kharkiv. The strikes come after US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that an "energy ceasefire" was in place between Russia and Ukraine. Russia's defence ministry said its "massive" strikes had targeted communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military. BBC Ukraine Correspondent Dan Johnson explains. title: Government Says It Helped Yandex Migrate Systems After Data Center Attacks
text: Government Says It Helped Yandex Migrate Systems After Data Center Attacks Oct. 14, 2026 REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova Russia’s Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev said Wednesday that his office helped tech giant Yandex migrate core systems to external backup servers following last week’s Ukrainian drone attacks. “The ministry assisted Yandex in providing additional sites for relocating key systems,” Shadayev told the business news outlet RBC. Yandex maintained that it has “for many years” developed distributed infrastructure and backup capacities at independent sites. Ukrainian drone attacks, which Shadayev referred to as “ unprecedented ,” damaged three of Yandex’s six data centers last week. The outages disrupted search, navigation, food delivery and banking services while also affecting corporate clients on Yandex Cloud, including retail giants like Lenta and Magnit. Key Yandex services like Pay and Cloud did not appear to be fully restored as of Wednesday evening. title: Nord Stream May Have Been Lawful Target, Argue Lawyers for Ukrainian Accused of Bombing
text: Nord Stream May Have Been Lawful Target, Argue Lawyers for Ukrainian Accused of Bombing By Reuters Oct. 14, 2026 Serhii K., a former Ukrainian army officer. Markus Scholz / Pool via REUTERS Lawyers for a Ukrainian ex-military officer accused of leading the bombing of Russia 's Nord Stream pipeline in September 2022 argued at the start of his trial in Germany on Wednesday that "an aggressor's infrastructure " may have been a lawful target . Serhii Kuznetsov is accused of leading a group of Ukrainian agents including divers and an explosives expert that blew up Russia 's largest gas pipeline to Europe in one of the biggest infrastructure sabotage operations of modern times. The case provides the first opportunity for a public hearing of evidence gathered during a years-long investigation, which has been diplomatically and politically awkward for a German government that remains staunchly supportive of Ukraine despite the investigative trail linking Kyiv to the bombing. title: Fire Spreads at Rostov Oil Terminal After Drone Attack
text: Fire Spreads at Rostov Oil Terminal After Drone Attack Oct. 14, 2026 @supernova_plus / Telegram Another storage tank exploded at an oil terminal in Russia’s southern city of Rostov-on-Don late Tuesday, as a fire sparked by a drone attack continued to burn for a fourth day, monitoring channels reported. The blaze at the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery’s terminal has spread to eight of its 12 storage tanks, the independent news outlet Astra reported . The Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova+ said another tank exploded late Tuesday. Footage from the site showed tanks engulfed in flames beneath columns of black smoke. The local Telegram channel Rostov Glavny reported a bright flash on the city’s left bank at 11:50 p.m. Tuesday. Drones struck the terminal, formerly known as Yug Rusi, in Rostov’s Zheleznodorozhny district overnight on Oct. 10. NASA’s FIRMS satellite monitoring system detected a fire at the site. news Rostov Oil Terminal Burns for Third Day After Reported Ukrainian Drone Attack Read more Authorities had not announced that the blaze had been extinguished as of Wednesday morning. title: Russia Announces Visas for Citizens of Montenegro in Reciprocal Move
text: Russia Announces Visas for Citizens of Montenegro in Reciprocal Move Oct. 14, 2026 Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Moskva News Agency Russia will introduce visa requirements for citizens of Montenegro in retaliation to Podgorica’s decision to end its bilateral visa-free travel agreement with Moscow as it seeks to join the EU in 2028. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova confirmed that Montenegro’s foreign ministry notified Moscow of its intent to cancel the 2008 mutual travel agreement on Sept. 28. “In practice, this means that starting Nov. 1, our citizens will only be able to enter and remain in Montenegro with visas. Accordingly, citizens of Montenegro will also have to obtain visas for trips to Russia,” Zakharova said. Montenegro announced in July that it would end visa-free access for citizens of Russia, Belarus, China, Saudi Arabia and Turkey to align with EU standards. Zakharova argued the decision would curb Russian tourism, harm local businesses and degrade Montenegro’s investment climate. title: Putin Convenes Top Russian Officials to Discuss Cybersecurity
text: Putin Convenes Top Russian Officials to Discuss Cybersecurity By Reuters Oct. 14, 2026 kremlin.ru Russia n President Vladimir Putin will discuss cybersecurity with top officials on Wednesday, the Kremlin said, describing it as an increasingly pressing issue but denying the meeting was prompted by a spate of Ukrainian drone attacks on Russia n data centers. "Artificial intelligence technologies bring many benefits and advantages, boosting efficiency. But at the same time, of course, attempts by various states to weaponize these new technologies... pose threats to entire sectors of any country's economy," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters. "Naturally, we are no exception, and we must be prepared for these challenges. That is why the president is holding this meeting today." news Ukraine’s Strikes on Yandex Data Centers, Explained Read more Peskov said the meeting was not connected with Ukrainian drone strikes in the past week on four Russia n data centers — three belonging to tech group Yandex and one to Sberbank. title: Russian Supreme Court Bans Ingush Sufi Muslim Order as ‘Extremist’
text: Russian Supreme Court Bans Ingush Sufi Muslim Order as ‘Extremist’ Oct. 14, 2026 right-partner.ru Russia’s Supreme Court on Wednesday outlawed the Batal Hajji brotherhood , a closed Sufi Muslim order originating from the North Caucasus republic of Ingushetia. The court granted a request from state prosecutors to designate the order as an “extremist” organization for “providing material support for bandit insurgents of the North Caucasus.” The Prosecutor General’s Office said Batal Hajji members were linked to numerous attacks on Russian police and military in the North Caucasus and orchestrated the deadly 2009 Nevsky Express train bombing claimed by Chechen rebel leader Doku Umarov. title: Latvia Formally Blacklists Russian Journalist Leonid Ragozin
text: Latvia Formally Blacklists Russian Journalist Leonid Ragozin Oct. 14, 2026 Leonid Ragozin. Social media Latvian authorities have formally declared Riga-based Russian journalist Leonid Ragozin persona non grata, local media reported, and Ragozin himself confirmed on Wednesday. Latvian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Līga Jermacāne told the outlet Delfi that an unidentified Russian national was added to the persona non grata list last Wednesday. Foreign Ministry adviser Toms Sadovskis said the basis for the decision will be withheld for “national security” reasons. On Wednesday, Ragozin confirmed that he was notified of his expulsion the day before. Ragozin claimed he was blacklisted in retaliation for his critical reporting and commentary on Western policy and far-right political networks. He argued that Latvia intentionally declared him persona non grata to prevent him from appealing his expulsion in Latvian courts. “For me it is a huge personal tragedy. I am being evicted from my only beloved home, deprived of my circle of friendship and support,” Ragozin posted on X. title: Russia Fumes as Top Gymnasts Blocked From World Championships in Netherlands
text: Russia Fumes as Top Gymnasts Blocked From World Championships in Netherlands Oct. 14, 2026 Angelina Melnikova. Yasuyoshi Chiba / AFP Russia has accused Dutch authorities of denying visas to three of Russia’s leading female gymnasts for the World Championships in Rotterdam, which kick off this weekend, and jeopardizing their qualification path for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Reigning world all-around champion Angelina Melnikova, Tokyo 2020 team Olympic champion Viktoria Listunova and 2026 European silver medalist Anna Kalmykova have all reportedly been refused visas, the Russian Gymnastics Federation said Tuesday, citing the Dutch Embassy in Moscow. The refusal notices apparently expressed diplomatic concerns, stating that “one or several Schengen member states consider the athletes a threat to their international relations.” “We view the actions of the Dutch authorities as a deliberate elimination of the strongest gymnasts from competition for world medals and Olympic quotas,” the Russian Gymnastics Federation said. title: Russia Arrests Japanese Journalist on Suspicion of Spying
text: Russia Arrests Japanese Journalist on Suspicion of Spying By Reuters Oct. 14, 2026 Screenshot / Russian Federal Security Service Russia said on Tuesday it had detained a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage and accused Tokyo of using media correspondents to gather intelligence, marking a new low in bilateral relations that have deteriorated sharply in recent months. Russia's Foreign Ministry identified the journalist as Yuki Imai and the FSB security agency said he worked for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, which is a regional newspaper for Japan's northern island. He was detained in the far eastern Sakhalin region the day before he planned to leave the country, the FSB said without specifying the date. It accused him of collecting and storing information on Russia's defense capabilities for intelligence purposes that it said could be used against Russian security. The Hokkaido Shimbun did not confirm the journalist's identity, saying only that it was still confirming details and that the reporter's safety was its top priority. title: Ukraine Accuses SpaceX of Crippling Drone Missions as Ties With U.S. Worsen
text: Ukraine Accuses SpaceX of Crippling Drone Missions as Ties With U.S. Worsen By Reuters Oct. 14, 2026 Mil.gov.ua Ukraine accused Elon Musk's SpaceX on Wednesday of limiting Starlink services, crippling its drones, as Russia n missiles knocked out power stations in attacks President Volodymyr Zelensky called "ostentatious disrespect" to Donald Trump. Kyiv's relationship with Washington has taken a sharp turn for the worse since U.S. President Trump abruptly lifted sanctions on Russia n diesel last week and publicly turned on Zelensky. Trump, under political pressure to lower fuel prices that have soared since he launched a war against Iran, has called on Kyiv to halt attacks on Russia n refineries, and said Ukrainians should replace their wartime leader. The U.S. president also announced that Ukraine and Russia had both agreed to halt attacks on energy targets, although neither side confirmed this and the past two days have seen intensive Russia n bombing, including of Ukrainian power stations. title: Russia’s Krasnodar Region Raises Alert as Oil Washes Ashore on Black Sea Coast
text: Russia’s Krasnodar Region Raises Alert as Oil Washes Ashore on Black Sea Coast Oct. 14, 2026 @lifeabrau / Telegram Authorities in Russia’s southern Krasnodar region have raised the alert level in Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk over an oil spill after fuel oil washed ashore and satellite images showed pollution spreading along the Black Sea coast. Governor Veniamin Kondratyev issued an order warning of a potential emergency in the two cities. He attributed the spill to “accidents” involving vessels targeted by Ukrainian naval drones on Oct. 6. The order calls for increased environmental monitoring and surveillance of potential industrial hazards. It also recommends that the regional branch of Russia’s Marine Rescue Service take measures to prevent oil from reaching the shoreline. Fuel oil has already been found along roughly 500 meters of coastline near Novorossiysk, the city’s chief rescue official, Alexei Oderov, said . Local residents have also reported pollution on the shore. Olga Kotlyar, head of the Abrau-Dyurso rural district, appealed for volunteers to help municipal workers clean up a beach. title: Ukrainian Drones Hit Sberbank Data Center After Yandex Attacks
text: Ukrainian Drones Hit Sberbank Data Center After Yandex Attacks Oct. 14, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram Ukrainian drones targeted a major data center under construction for Russian state lender Sberbank in the Saratov region overnight, First Deputy CEO Alexander Vedyakhin said Wednesday, as attacks on Moscow disrupted more than 500 flights. Vedyakhin said all banking systems and online services continued to operate normally and no employees were injured in the attack in the Volga River city of Balakovo, according to the state-run news agency TASS. Users across Russia nevertheless reported disruptions to Sberbank and its GigaChat artificial intelligence service, as well as several other major online platforms, according to outage tracker Detector404. The reports did not establish a link between the disruptions and the drone attacks. NASA’s satellite fire-monitoring system showed multiple fires in Balakovo. Saratov region Governor Roman Busargin said “all infrastructure facilities” were operating normally, without identifying Sberbank’s data center as a target.
